quote_zh: 向反应瓶中加入叔丁醇200mL，开动搅拌，室温下将4.1g金属钾(99％，0.105mol)加入其中，待金属钾溶解完全后，控制釜温在25℃，将34.8g  2-氯-3-溴甲基-4-甲磺酰基苯甲酸甲酯(98％，0.1mol)倒入釜中进行碱解反应
arithmetic_check: Charges. Potassium metal 4.1 g at 99 percent stated as 0.105 mol: K = 39.10, so 0.105 mol is 4.11 g of potassium, which at the printed 99 percent strength needs 4.15 g of charge against the 4.1 g printed, and read the other way 4.1 g x 0.99 / 39.10 = 0.1038 mol against 0.105 mol printed. The gap is 1.1 percent and is within the rounding of a mass printed to one decimal, so no molar_mass_inconsistent is raised. Methyl 2-chloro-3-(bromomethyl)-4-(methanesulfonyl)benzoate 34.8 g at 98 percent stated as 0.1 mol: C10H10BrClO4S = 341.60, so 0.1 mol is 34.16 g pure and 34.86 g at 98 percent against 34.8 g printed, correct to 0.2 percent. Product closure. No mass and no yield are printed for the potassium salt, which is never isolated, so there is nothing to close on this step: the only figure is the in-process normalised content of 98.1 percent, and the 0.1 mol carried into step (2) is the same molar amount as the ester charged here. Both printed pairs close against the compounds named, so neither mass_balance_implausible nor molar_mass_inconsistent is raised, and no number has been adjusted.

quote_zh: 向反应釜中加入130mL  DMF、10.8g  2-四氢呋喃甲醇(99％，0.105mol)和14.1g叔丁醇钾(95％，0.12mol)，开动搅拌，控制釜温在10℃，将步骤(1)制备得到的2-氯-3-溴甲基-4-甲磺酰基苯甲酸钾盐(98.1％，0.1mol)分八次加入反应瓶中，总加料时间为3h，加毕保温反应4h
arithmetic_check: Charges. Tetrahydrofurfuryl alcohol 10.8 g at 99 percent stated as 0.105 mol: C5H10O2 = 102.13, so 0.105 mol is 10.72 g pure and 10.83 g at 99 percent against 10.8 g printed, correct. Potassium tert-butoxide 14.1 g at 95 percent stated as 0.12 mol: C4H9OK = 112.21, so 0.12 mol is 13.47 g pure and 14.18 g at 95 percent against 14.1 g printed, correct to 0.6 percent, and read the other way 14.1 g x 0.95 / 112.21 = 0.1194 mol against 0.12 mol printed. The benzoate salt is charged as 0.1 mol at 98.1 percent with no mass printed, so no molecular weight can be tested on it. Product closure. Limiting input 0.1 mol as printed, or 0.0998 mol taken from the step (1) ester charge; product C14H17ClO6S = 348.80; 33.0 g of solid assaying 96.8 percent is 31.94 g of the target compound, which is 0.0916 mol, that is 91.6 percent on the printed 0.1 mol and 91.7 percent on the 0.0998 mol the ester charge actually gives, against the printed 91.8 percent. The residual gap is 0.1 to 0.2 percentage points; the printed figure is reproduced exactly if the assay is read as 97.0 percent rather than 96.8, or if a slightly lower molecular weight is used, so the difference sits inside the rounding of a mass printed to one decimal and an assay printed to one decimal. It is recorded here rather than flagged: no mass_balance_implausible and no molar_mass_inconsistent is raised, and nothing has been changed. The printed yield is explicitly a two-step figure on the methyl ester of step (1), which was itself charged at 0.1 mol, so the basis is consistent. Continuity: step (1) delivered 0.1 mol of the salt and this step charges 0.1 mol of it, so no scale_discontinuity.

The drawing agrees with the prose on the substrate, the alcohol, the base, the alkali metal and the product, so no drawing_text_conflict and no reagent_drawn_not_written; the HCl drawn under the arrow is the workup acidification the prose describes and is recorded in workup rather than as a reagent. The DMF medium and the workup water are on no arrow, but they take no part in the transformation, so no reagent_written_not_drawn. The drawn product carries no stereo bond, so the (RS) in the name comes from the prose alone.
